sentences.text: This petition under section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashment of FIR No. 30/2023 registered at P.S. Raoji Bazar, Indore for the offence under sections 420, 467 and 468 of IPC and the subsequent proceedings thereto.

Facts necessary for disposal of this petition in brief are that aforesaid impugned FIR has been lodged at the behest of complaint Smt. Sudha W/o Datturao Panwar on the allegation that applicant has forged and fabricated the documents for encroaching upon 350 sq.ft. of vacant land which is part of her House No. 5/2 Moti Tabela, Indore.
2. Counsel for applicant submits that applicant is validly occupying and possessing plot No. 5/2 with construction thereon admeasuring 350 sq.ft. at Moti Tabela, Indore.
To grab the validly own property of the applicant, the complainant is strenuously making efforts since long back and allegedly made false complaint against the applicant.

Counsel further submits that in the year 2013,
a report under section 145 of Cr.P.C. was filed before the SDO, Juni Indore wherein applicant 2 MCRC-28986-2024 and complainant Smt. Sudha were party to the proceedings.
In the aforesaid proceedings on 19.11.2014 final order was passed by the SDO.
Being aggrieved by the order

,
applicant preferred Cr.Rev.No. 958/2014.
Learned Revisional court by order dated 11.3.2016 (Annx.P/3) allowed the revision in favour of the applicant.
It has been held in the aforesaid order that applicant Anwar Khan is in possession of the disputed land from much earlier to 8.10.2012 and on this ground, the order passed by the SDO was set aside.
Learned counsel further submits that prosecution could not file even a single document which has allegedly been fabricated by the applicant.

The dispute between the complainant and applicant with regard to ownership and possession of House No. 5/2 at Moti Tabela, Indore is purely a civil dispute which has been given criminal colour and impugned FIR has been maliciously filed for wreaking vengeance against the present applicant.

sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that even if the FIR is taken to its face value, no offence is made out against the applicant.

Learned counsel has placed reliance on paragraph Nos.102 and 103 of the judgment of Hon. Apex Court in the case of State of Haryana Vs. Bhajanlal, 1992 Supp(1) SCC 335 which is reproduced below :-
"102 I n the backdrop of the interpretation of the various relevant provisions of the Code under Chapter XIV and of the principles of Jaw enunciated by this Court in a series of decisions relating to the exercise of the extra-ordinary power under Article 226 or the inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code wh' '.; we have extracted and repro- duced above, we give the following categories of cases by way of illustration wherein such power could be exercised either to prevent abuse of the process of any Court or otherwise to secure the ends of E justice, though it may not be possible to lay down any precise, clearly defined and sufficiently channelised and inflexible guidelines or rigid formulae and to give an exhaustive list of myriad kinds of cases wherein such power should be exercised.
1. Where the allegations made in the First Information Report F or the complaint,
even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima-facie constitute any off- 3 MCRC-28986-2024 ence or make out a case against the accused.

sentences.text: 2. Where the allegations in the First Information Report and other materials, if any, accompanying the F.l.R. do not disclose G a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under Section 156( 1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.

3. Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.

4. Where, the allegations in the F.I.R. do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under Section 155(2) of the Code.

5. Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

6. Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the concerned Act (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the concerned Act,
providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

103 We also give a note of caution to the effect that the power of quashing a criminal proceeding should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection and that too in the rarest of rare cases;
that the Court will not be justified in embarking upon an enquiry as to thep reliability or genuineness or otherwise of the alleg~tions made in the F.I.R. or the complaint and that the extraordinary or inherent powers do not confer an arbitrary jurisdiction on the Court to act according to its whim or caprice."

Learned counsel further placed reliance on the judgment of Apex Court in the case of Rajib Ranjan and others Vs. R.Vijay Kumar, (2015) 1 SCC 513 (paragraph Nos.19 to 26).

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for complainant has opposed the prayer on the ground that applicant has taken different stands before different forums with regard to ownership of the disputed land.
Patta relied upon by the counsel has not been 4 MCRC-28986-2024 issued by concerned authority.
No document with regard to ownership of the disputed land in favour of applicant has been produced.
On these miscellaneous contentions, learned court urges the Court to dismiss the petition.
4. Learned counsel for State supporting the complainant has also opposed the prayer made by counsel for applicant.

5. Heard learned counsel for parties and perused the record.
6.
From perusal of the impugned FIR (Annx.P/1) it is manifest that much span of time from 26.6.1987 to 2.2.2023 has been given for commission of offence by the applicant.

Neither before the SDO in proceedings under section 145 Cr.P.C. nor before the Sessions Court in Cr.Rev.No. 958/2014 it has been contended that applicant has forged the document with respect to disputed land for grabbing it.
The complainant could not point out the date when the applicant encroached upon the disputed land.
In para 24 of the Criminal Revision, it has been given the finding that possession by the applicant over the disputed land is very much earlier preceding to 8.10.2012.
It is also undisputed that civil proceedings are pending between the complainant and the applicant.
FIR has been registered on 2.2.2023 but till date the respondent/State could not even suggest the document which has been found forged by the applicant.

Mere an allegation in the FIR with regard to forgery cannot be accepted unless it is supported by some evidence produced wither at the time of filing of FIR or through evidence collected during investigation.

There should be a little deeper scrutiny into the circumstances under which the complaint came to be filed would demonstrate that allegation of fabricating the false record is clearly an afterthought and it becomes more than apparent that the respondent has chosen to level such a make belief allegation with sole motive to give a shape of criminality to the entire dispute, which was otherwise civil in nature.
No expert opinion with regard to forging the document 5 MCRC-28986-2024 has been obtained and placed on record.

It will be sheer abuse of process of law if the prosecution is allowed to continue based on the allegations in Anwar Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2113346/

The applicant is discharged of the offence under section 420, 467 and 468 IPC.
